threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the tube' instead of 'the underground'. A dead giveaway that you haven’t mastered the local lingo yet.
Caught a night bus from Brixton to Clapham, driver had a Spotify playlist that was all 90s R&B. Everyone was vibing, even the rowdy teens up front.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a cat lounging on a beer crate outside the Späti, while a group of artists debated over kombucha recipes. That's Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you see a party breaking out at the canal with an impromptu DJ, while old ladies walk their dogs just a few meters away without a care.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a true local by how they navigate the BART delays—none of this ‘I’ll wait for the next train’ nonsense. It’s all about the bus and dodging the tourists.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 31 in the Tenderloin, and a guy started serenading the whole bus. Half the passengers were nodding along; the other half seemed confused. Classic SF moment.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all tapas are created equal, but locals know a good esgarrat requires perfect, tender escalivada. It’s the little things.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can usually tell by their confusion over how to order pa amb tomàquet—asking if it comes as a side with everything.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think a ‘short walk’ means 10 minutes, not 30. And you avoid the footbridge over the river like it's a London Marathon on a Sunday.
Caught a whiff of jerk chicken on the 196 last night, only to find a guy with a saxophone playing along. Best £1.75 I ever spent.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The sound of a random street musician mixing techno with folk tunes outside my window at 2 AM—only in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a spontaneous techno party in a laundromat at 2 AM, complete with a DJ and dancers spinning while clothes tumble.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by how they navigate BART delays. A tourist panics, but a local just shrugs and knows the bus is even worse.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a full tuxedo get on the 31, sipping a coffee like it was a wedding reception. Only in SF do you see wedding attire on the way to work.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think they can just stroll into a plaça and find a seat. Local families have claimed them by 9 AM for the entire day!

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They still get flustered at the absurdity of the bus schedules, checking their phones every two minutes, while the locals just roll their eyes and wait.
